title: Focus chain algorithm and firing focus events
body:
### What is the issue with the HTML Standard?

I read the section on focusing and created the following script locally:

**index.html**
```html
<style>
  body {
	display: flex;
	flex-direction: column;
	align-items: flex-start;
  }
  iframe {
	border-width: 5px;
  }
</style>
<input id='input' type='text'>
<iframe src="main-iframe.html"></iframe>
<script>
setTimeout(() => {
	let secondWindow = frames[0]
	let thirdWindow = frames[0].frames[0];
	
	let dictionary = {
		window, 
		secondWindow, 
		thirdWindow
	};
	
	for (let [key, value] of Object.entries(dictionary)) {
		value.addEventListener("focus", (e) => {
			console.log(e.type, key, e);
		})
		value.frames[0]?.frameElement.addEventListener("focus", (e) => {
			console.log(e.type, key+":iframeElement", e);
		})
		value.input.addEventListener("focus", (e) => {
			console.log(e.type, key+":input", e);
		})
	}
	let secondWindowFrameButton = document.createElement("button");
	secondWindowFrameButton.onclick = () => secondWindow.frames[0].frameElement.focus();
	secondWindowFrameButton.textContent = "secondWindow.frames[0].frameElement.focus()"
	
	let thirdWindowFrameInputButton = document.createElement("button");
	thirdWindowFrameInputButton.onclick = () => thirdWindow.input.focus();
	thirdWindowFrameInputButton.textContent = "thirdWindow.input.focus()";
	
	document.body.append(secondWindowFrameButton, thirdWindowFrameInputButton);
	console.log("timeout fired");
}, 1000)
</script>
```

**main-frame.html**
```html
<style>
  iframe {
	border-width: 5px;
  }
</style>
<input id='input' type='text'>
<iframe src="source.html"></iframe>
```

**source.html**
```html
<input id='input' type='text'>
```

**Expectation:** When we click on the input in `<iframe src="source.html"></iframe>`, at least 5 `"focus"` events should appear in the console.

**Reality:** In the latest versions of both Firefox and Chrome, you only get 2 `"focus"` events. Why?

---

The specification contains a key algorithm called the [focus chain](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/interaction.html#focus-chain):

> The [focus chain](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/interaction.html#focus-chain) of a [focusable area](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/interaction.html#focusable-area) subject is the ordered list constructed as follows:
> 
> 1. Let output be an empty [list](https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#list).
> 2. Let currentObject be subject.
> 3. While true:
>    1. [Append](https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#list-append) currentObject to output.
>    2. If currentObject is an [area](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/image-maps.html#the-area-element) element's shape, then [append](https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#list-append) that [area](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/image-maps.html#the-area-element) element to output.
>    
>       Otherwise, if currentObject's [DOM anchor](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/interaction.html#dom-anchor) is an element that is not currentObject itself, then [append](https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#list-append) currentObject's [DOM anchor](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/interaction.html#dom-anchor) to output.
> 
>    3. If currentObject is a [focusable area](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/interaction.html#focusable-area), then set currentObject to currentObject's [DOM anchor](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/interaction.html#dom-anchor)'s [node document](https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-node-document).
> 
>       Otherwise, if currentObject is a [Document](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/dom.html#document) whose [node navigable](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/document-sequences.html#node-navigable)'s [parent](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/document-sequences.html#nav-parent) is non-null, then set currentObject to currentObject's [node navigable](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/document-sequences.html#node-navigable)'s [parent](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/document-sequences.html#nav-parent).
> 
>       Otherwise, [break](https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#iteration-break).
> 
> 4. Return output.

> Note: The chain starts with subject and (if subject is or can be the [currently focused area of a top-level traversable](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/interaction.html#currently-focused-area-of-a-top-level-traversable)) continues up the focus hierarchy up to the [Document](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/dom.html#document) of the [top-level traversable](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/document-sequences.html#top-level-traversable).

Based on this algorithm, what would the [focus chain](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/interaction.html#focus-chain) be for `input` inside `<iframe src="source.html"></iframe>`?
My guess is what the [focus chain](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/interaction.html#focus-chain) looks like in this case: `[input, document, iframe, document, iframe, document]`.

In the [focus update steps](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/interaction.html#focus-update-steps) algorithm:

> 1. If the last entry in old chain and the last entry in new chain are the same, pop the last entry from old chain and the last entry from new chain and redo this step.
> 
> ...
> 
> 4. For each entry entry in new chain, in reverse order, run these substeps:
>     1. If entry is a [focusable area](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/interaction.html#focusable-area), and the [focused area of the document](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/interaction.html#focused-area-of-the-document) is not entry:
>           1. Set document's [relevant global object](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/webappapis.html#concept-relevant-global)'s [navigation API](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/nav-history-apis.html#window-navigation-api)'s [focus changed during ongoing navigation](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/nav-history-apis.html#focus-changed-during-ongoing-navigation) to true.
>           2. Designate entry as the [focused area of the document](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/interaction.html#focused-area-of-the-document).
>     2. If entry is an element, let focus event target be entry.
>     
>         If entry is a [Document](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/dom.html#document) object, let focus event target be that [Document](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/dom.html#document) object's [relevant global object](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/webappapis.html#concept-relevant-global).
> 
>        Otherwise, let focus event target be null.
> 
>    3. If entry is the last entry in new chain, and entry is an [Element](https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#interface-element), and the last entry in old chain is also an [Element](https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#interface-element), then let related focus target be the last entry in old chain. Otherwise, let related focus target be null.
>    4. If focus event target is not null, [fire a focus event](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/interaction.html#fire-a-focus-event) named [focus](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/indices.html#event-focus) at focus event target, with related focus target as the related target.

> Note: In some cases, e.g. if entry is an [area](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/image-maps.html#the-area-element) element's shape, a scrollable region, or a [viewport](https://drafts.csswg.org/css2/#viewport), no event is fired.

The first step of the algorithm can shorten our new [focus chain](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/interaction.html#focus-chain) (if the old [focus chain](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/interaction.html#focus-chain) has matching chain elements from the end of the list).
Next, we look at the loop where a [fire a focus event](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/interaction.html#fire-a-focus-event) with the name `"focus"` occurs. The [fire a focus event](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/interaction.html#fire-a-focus-event) will only occur if the `focus event target` is not `null` (that is, it is either an `element` or a `Document`).

Thus, given a [focus chain](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/interaction.html#focus-chain) that looks like this: `[input, document, iframe, document, iframe, document]`, we should receive one `focus` event on the `input` element (which will be the last one, since we use reverse enumeration of chain elements), two `focus` events on the `window` elements (since the document elements will be converted to `window`, specifically two, not three, due to the first step in the [focus update steps](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/interaction.html#focus-update-steps)) and two `focus` events on the `iframe` elements.

**Call order:**
 - `iframe`
 - `window`
 - `iframe`
 - `window`
 - `input`

If I interpreted the spec correctly, neither Firefox nor Chrome implement this behavior. The most interesting thing is that they also invoke these events differently.

For example, in Chrome, if you click the `secondWindow.frames[0].frameElement.focus()` button, you will see:
 - `secondWindow`
 - `thirdWindow`
 - `secondWindow:iframeElement`

In Firefox:
 - `thirdWindow`

**How I think it should be:**
 - `window:iframe`
 - `secondWindow`
 - `thirdWindow` (not `secondWindow:iframeElement`)

If we click it again, no events will occur in Chrome, but in Firefox it will be the same as the first time:
- `thirdWindow`

Now, if we refresh the page for the sake of clarity after the first test and check for clicks on the `thirdWindow.input.focus()` button, Chrome will display this:
 - `thirdWindow`
 - `thirdWindow:input`

In Firefox:
 - `thirdWindow`
 - `thirdWindow:input`

**How I think it should be:**
 - `window:iframeElement`
 - `secondWindow`
 - `secondWindow:iframeElement`
 - `thirdWindow`
 - `thirdWindow:input`

Clicking it again doesn't change anything in either browser.

Specifiers are needed to explain this.

@rakina @annevk @domenic
